definition_zh: 笔记；便条；音符；注意；记下
definition_en: a short written record or message; a single musical sound; attention; and the act of noticing or writing something down
core_image: 纸页边缘写满小字，一张折好的短笺压在书页之间
scene: 厨房的桌上压着一张折好的纸条，字迹很急，末尾没有署名。She read the note twice before answering.
sceneCN: 这里是「便条、短笺」（第 2 个义项：写在纸上的简短留言），句意为她把那张便条读了两遍才回话。图中可辨识物件：折好的纸条、厨房桌、笔。

derivatives.zh: 由 note 与 book 复合而成，义为「笔记本」
由 note 的拉丁词干加 -able 构成，义为「值得注意的；显著的」
由拉丁词干 notare 加 -tion 构成，义为「记号系统；记谱法」

senses.title: A short written record of something heard or read
senses.definition: a short written record, especially of what a speaker said or what a reader wants to remember
senses.definitionCN: 简短的书面记录，尤指记下讲者所说或读者想记住的内容
senses.example: She filled three pages with notes during the lecture.
senses.exampleCN: 讲座期间她记满了三页笔记。
senses.why: Latin nota was a mark or written sign, and the first English sense kept that idea of a small written trace left behind for later use.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 nota 是「记号、写下的符号」，英语最初的意思保留了这种「为以后使用而留下的小小书写痕迹」。

senses.title: A short written message
senses.definition: a short informal letter or message written on a piece of paper
senses.definitionCN: 写在纸上的简短、非正式的留言或信
senses.example: She read the note twice before answering.
senses.exampleCN: 她把那张便条读了两遍才回话。
senses.why: Because any written mark can be handed to someone else, note slid from a private record to a message left for another person, usually brief and casual.
senses.whyCN: 既然任何书写记号都能交给别人，note 就从私人记录滑向留给别人的留言，通常简短而随意。

senses.title: A single musical sound or its written sign
senses.definition: a single sound in music, or the written symbol that stands for it
senses.definitionCN: 音乐中的单个音，或代表这个音的书写符号
senses.example: She held the last note longer than the others.
senses.exampleCN: 她把最后一个音拖得比别的音更长。
senses.why: A musical tone can be written down like any other sign, so the word for a written mark came to name one printed dot on a staff and then the sound it stands for.
senses.whyCN: 乐音也能像别的符号一样写下来，于是表示书写记号的词先指谱线中的一个点，再指它所代表的那个音。

senses.title: Attention or notice given to something
senses.definition: attention given to something, especially in the phrase take note of
senses.definitionCN: 对某事给予的关注，尤用于 take note of 这一说法
senses.example: Take note of the small changes in the pattern.
senses.exampleCN: 请留意这个图案里细微的变化。
senses.why: A note is something you write so that it will be remembered, and from that comes the sense of giving something enough attention for it to be remembered.
senses.whyCN: 笔记是为了日后记得才写下的东西，由此引申出「给予足够关注、以便记住」的意思。

senses.title: To notice or write something down
senses.definition: to notice something and give it attention, or to write it down so that it is recorded
senses.definitionCN: 注意到某事并加以关注，或把它写下来留作记录
senses.example: He noted the time in the margin of his notebook.
senses.exampleCN: 他把时间记在笔记本的页边。
senses.why: Once the noun means a written trace of attention, the matching verb naturally means the act that produces it, so noting is both watching closely and setting the result on paper.
senses.whyCN: 当名词已经表示「注意力留下的书写痕迹」，与之对应的动词自然就表示产生这个痕迹的动作，所以 noting 既是仔细观察，也是把结果落到纸上。

intro.en: Note comes from a Latin word for a mark or written sign, entered English through Old French, and later grew senses for messages, music and attention.
intro.cn: note 来自拉丁语中表示「记号、书写符号」的词，经古法语进入英语，后来才长出留言、音乐与注意等义项。

items.en: Nota was a mark, a written character or a sign of something, and it is generally connected with the Latin verb for knowing, noscere.
items.cn: nota 是记号、书写符号或某事的标志，一般认为它与拉丁语中表示「认识」的动词 noscere 有关。

items.en: The verb notare meant to mark, to write down or to observe, and it supplied the family of words about noting and notation.
items.cn: 动词 notare 意为标记、写下或观察，由此衍生出与记录和记号系统有关的一族词。

items.en: Old French passed on note as a written mark, a memorandum or a short writing after the Norman period.
items.cn: 诺曼时期之后，古法语把 note 传进英语，意思为书面的记号、备忘或短小的文字。

items.en: Middle English note covered a written record, a melody and a token of something, so the musical sense was already present.
items.cn: 中古英语的 note 已包含书面记录、曲调与某事物的标志，音乐义那时就已经在场。

items.en: Modern English adds the short message, the musical symbol, the sense of attention and the verb, together with the compound banknote for paper money.
items.cn: 现代英语增添了便条、音乐符号、注意等意思和动词用法，还添上表示纸币的复合词 banknote。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin stem nota through English derivatives; the near-meaning group collects the short writings and messages that note resembles.
note.cn: 形近组沿拉丁词干 nota 收英语派生词；近义组收与 note 相近的短小文字与留言。

entries.definition: A system of written symbols, such as the notation used for music.
entries.definitionCN: 书写符号的系统，如音乐所用的记谱法。

entries.definition: Worthy of attention, built from the same stem with -able.
entries.definitionCN: 值得注意的，同一词干加 -able 构成。

entries.definition: A book of blank pages for writing notes.
entries.definitionCN: 用来记笔记、带空白页的本子。

entries.definition: A short written message inside an office or organization.
entries.definitionCN: 办公室或机构内部简短的书面留言。

entries.definition: Information sent from one person to another, in speech, writing or another medium.
entries.definitionCN: 由一人传给另一人的信息，可用口头、书面或其他方式。

entries.definition: A written or stored account of something kept for later reference.
entries.definitionCN: 为日后查阅而保存的书面或存储记载。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Latin mark that became a small piece of writing, then a message, a musical sign and a act of attention.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词原是拉丁语的「记号」，后来变成一小段文字、一条留言、一个音乐符号，以及一次关注的动作。

normal.en: Latin nota meant a mark or written sign, so every sense of note still involves something set down to be seen again.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 nota 意为记号或书写符号，所以 note 的每个义项都离不开「写下来以便再看」这件事。

normal.en: Notare is the Latin verb to mark or write, and it is the base of notation and notable.
normal.cn: notare 是拉丁语里「标记、书写」的动词，也是 notation 与 notable 的底座。

normal.en: The musical note is simply a written sign on a staff, which is why the same word names the symbol and the sound.
normal.cn: 音乐里的 note 不过是谱线上的一个书写符号，所以同一个词既指符号也指声音。

normal.en: Take note of keeps the physical picture: you write something because you want to keep it in mind.
normal.cn: take note of 保留了那个具体画面：你把它写下来，是因为想把它记在心里。

normal.en: Banknote is a note in the old sense of a written promise to pay, now the paper money itself.
normal.cn: banknote 里的 note 用的是旧义「书面的付款承诺」，今天则直接指那张纸币。

abstract.en: A mark that was meant to be read later became a message meant for someone else, and both still depend on paper holding a thought still.
abstract.cn: 一个本来留给以后自己看的记号，变成了留给别人的留言，两者都依赖纸张把一个念头固定住。

abstract.en: Note shows how writing turns attention into an object: what you noticed becomes something you can hand over.
abstract.cn: note 展示了书写如何把注意力变成物件：你注意到的东西变成可以递交出去的东西。

abstract.en: The same short word can be a page of study, a line of music and a warning, because all three are traces left for a later reader.
abstract.cn: 同一个短词可以是整页的学习、一行音乐，也可以是一句提醒，因为三者都是留给后来读者看的痕迹。

examples.en: She read the note twice before answering.
examples.cn: 她把那张便条读了两遍才回话。

examples.en: She filled three pages with notes during the lecture.
examples.cn: 讲座期间她记满了三页笔记。

examples.en: He noted the time in the margin of his notebook.
examples.cn: 他把时间记在笔记本的页边。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「诺特」——桌上压着一张小纸条，几行字就说明了来意；note 就是便条、笔记。

root: 拉丁语 nota（记号、书写符号）与动词 notare（标记、写下），经古法语 note 进入中古英语；同族词有 notable、notation、notebook。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a written mark kept for later; the senses then divide into the record, the message, the musical sign, and attention with its verb.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「为日后而留下的书写记号」；义项由此分出记录、留言、音乐符号，以及注意和相应的动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a page crowded with small handwriting, with a folded slip pressed between the leaves.
core.cn: 核心意象：写满小字的纸页，夹着一张折好的短笺。

branches.en: a page of lecture notes written in a tight hand
branches.cn: 写得密密麻麻的一页讲座笔记

branches.en: a sentence underlined twice in the margin
branches.cn: 页边被划了两道线的句子

branches.en: a folded slip left on a kitchen table
branches.cn: 厨房桌上留下的折好的纸条

branches.en: one held tone at the end of a song
branches.cn: 歌曲结尾一个被拖长的音

branches.en: a reader pausing, then writing a date in the corner
branches.cn: 读者停了一下，在角上写下日期

intro.en: The word rests on a Latin noun for a mark, its verb, and English endings that build its derivatives and compounds.
intro.cn: 这个词立在拉丁语表示「记号」的名词与动词上，再由英语词尾构成它的派生词与复合词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin noun nota and its verb notare are the recorded source of this word family, so the Latin entries below are its direct ancestors.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语名词 nota 与动词 notare 是这个词族有记录的来源，因此下面的拉丁词条是它的直系祖先。

definition_zh: 没有什么；没有东西；无关紧要的事；零
definition_en: not anything at all; something too small to matter; and a score of zero in a game
core_image: 抽屉拉开，里面空空的，只有一层薄灰在光里浮动
scene: 抽屉被整个拉开，里面空空的，只有一层薄灰在光里浮动。The drawer was empty, and there was nothing inside but a layer of dust.
sceneCN: 这里是「没有什么、没有东西」（第 1 个义项：一样东西都不存在），句意为抽屉是空的，里面除了一层灰什么也没有。图中可辨识物件：拉开的抽屉、薄灰、窗光。

derivatives.zh: 由 nothing 加 -ness（性质、状态）构成，义为「虚无；空无」
由 good for nothing 固定成词，义为「无用的人」

senses.title: Not anything at all
senses.definition: not a single thing, used when absolutely nothing exists, happens or is present
senses.definitionCN: 一样东西也没有，用于表示完全不存在、不发生或不在场
senses.example: The drawer was empty, and there was nothing inside but a layer of dust.
senses.exampleCN: 抽屉是空的，里面除了一层灰什么也没有。
senses.why: Old English joined nān, meaning not one, to þing, meaning thing, so the word literally says not one thing and still carries that flat emptiness.
senses.whyCN: 古英语把表示「一个也不」的 nān 与表示「东西」的 þing 拼在一起，所以这个词字面上说的是「一样东西也没有」，至今仍带着那种空荡。

senses.title: Something too small or unimportant to matter
senses.titleCN: 无关紧要的事；微不足道的东西
senses.definition: a person or thing of no importance, or a remark or event that matters very little
senses.definitionCN: 不重要的人或事，或价值极小的言论与事件
senses.example: They argued for an hour over nothing.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为一件无关紧要的事争了一个小时。
senses.why: If a thing is nothing, it is not worth counting, so the word easily shifts from absence to worthlessness, especially when people want to dismiss a complaint.
senses.whyCN: 如果一件事是 nothing，就等于不值得计算，于是这个词很容易从「不存在」转到「不值得」，尤其是在人们想打发一句抱怨的时候。

senses.title: A score of zero in a game
senses.definition: zero as a score, especially in sports and games
senses.definitionCN: 比赛或游戏中的零分
senses.example: The match ended three to nothing.
senses.exampleCN: 比赛以三比零结束。
senses.why: A team with no runs has literally scored nothing, so the word for no thing became the name of the zero on the scoreboard.
senses.whyCN: 一支没有得分的队，字面上就是「什么也没得到」，于是表示「无物」的词成了记分牌上那个零的名称。

intro.en: Nothing is a native English compound of a negative word for not one and the noun for thing, and it contracted into a single pronoun in Old English.
intro.cn: nothing 是英语本土的复合词，由一个表示「一个也不」的否定词与表示「东西」的名词组成，在古英语里就已缩合成一个代词。

items.en: Nān was ne plus ān, not one, and it denied even a single item rather than merely denying a quality.
items.cn: nān 是 ne 加 ān，意为「一个也不」，它连单独一样东西都否定，而不只是否定某种性质。

items.en: Þing meant a thing, a matter or an assembly, and it supplied the noun half of the compound.
items.cn: þing 意为东西、事情或议事会，为这个复合词提供了名词那一半。

items.en: The two words were written together as nānþing and behaved as a single pronoun meaning no thing at all.
items.cn: 两个词被写在一起作 nānþing，像一个代词那样使用，意为「一样东西也没有」。

items.en: Middle English respelled the compound with not and thing, matching the shortened negator, and the old nān disappeared from it.
items.cn: 中古英语用 not 与 thing 重拼这个复合词，与缩短的否定词保持一致，旧的 nān 从中消失。

items.en: Modern English keeps nothing as a pronoun and a noun, and fixed phrases such as nothing but and for nothing carry the old emptiness into idiom.
items.cn: 现代英语让 nothing 兼作代词与名词，nothing but、for nothing 这类固定说法把古老的「空」带进了成语。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the other thing-pronouns built on the same pattern; the near-meaning group collects the words English uses for none and zero.
note.cn: 形近组收按同一模式造出的其他 thing 代词；近义组收英语里表示「无」与「零」的词。

entries.definition: A pronoun for any thing at all, built on the same thing element.
entries.definitionCN: 表示「任何东西」的代词，用了同一个 thing 成分。

entries.definition: A pronoun for one unspecified thing, the positive partner of nothing.
entries.definitionCN: 表示某个不指定东西的代词，是 nothing 的肯定对应词。

entries.definition: The noun inside nothing, meaning an object, matter or event.
entries.definitionCN: nothing 里的那个名词，意为物体、事情或事件。

entries.definition: Not one, or not any, used when a quantity is zero.
entries.definitionCN: 一个也不、任何也不，用于数量为零时。

entries.definition: The number that stands for no quantity at all.
entries.definitionCN: 表示完全没有数量的那个数字。

entries.definition: Nothing, especially a zero score in sports and records.
entries.definitionCN: 无，尤指体育与记录中的零分。

normalIntro.en: The word is not one plus thing, and its later senses keep asking what counts as a thing worth having.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是「一个也没有」加「东西」，它后来的义项一直在追问：什么才算值得拥有的东西。

normal.en: Nothing is nān plus þing: not one thing, so the word itself explains its own emptiness.
normal.cn: nothing 是 nān 加 þing：一样东西也没有，词本身就把自己的空说清楚了。

normal.en: The same nān is behind no and none, which is why all three refuse a quantity.
normal.cn: 同一个 nān 也藏在 no 与 none 后面，所以这三者都在拒绝某个数量。

normal.en: Middle English respelled the compound with not, linking nothing to the history of not.
normal.cn: 中古英语用 not 重拼这个复合词，把 nothing 与 not 的历史连在一起。

normal.en: Nothing but means only, because everything else has been excluded.
normal.cn: nothing but 意为「只有」，因为其余的一切都被排除掉了。

normal.en: For nothing means either free or wasted, and both say that no payment or result came back.
normal.cn: for nothing 既可以是「免费」，也可以是「白费」，两者都说没有回报或没有结果。

abstract.en: A word made of not one and thing turns absence into a noun, so English can talk about emptiness as if it were an object.
abstract.cn: 一个由「一个也不」和「东西」构成的词，把缺席变成了名词，于是英语能像谈论物件一样谈论空。

abstract.en: When nothing also means unimportant, the language quietly ranks existence by worth.
abstract.cn: 当 nothing 也指「不重要」，语言就在悄悄按价值给存在排位。

abstract.en: On a scoreboard nothing is a number, which shows how easily a word for absence can be counted.
abstract.cn: 在记分牌上 nothing 是一个数字，这说明表示「无」的词多么容易被计数。

examples.en: The drawer was empty, and there was nothing inside but a layer of dust.
examples.cn: 抽屉是空的，里面除了一层灰什么也没有。

examples.en: They argued for an hour over nothing.
examples.cn: 他们为一件无关紧要的事争了一个小时。

examples.en: The match ended three to nothing.
examples.cn: 比赛以三比零结束。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「那辛」——拉开抽屉，里面空空如也，什么也没有；nothing 就是没有什么。

root: 古英语 nān（ne 加 ān，一个也不）与 þing（东西）合成 nānþing，中古英语重拼为 nothing；与 not 同出这一否定词源，英语中没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is not one thing; it then extends to what is not worth counting and to the zero on a scoreboard.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「一样东西也没有」；义项由此扩展到不值得计算的东西，以及记分牌上的零。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an open drawer that is completely empty except for a thin layer of dust.
core.cn: 核心意象：拉开的抽屉空空如也，只有一层薄灰。

branches.en: an empty drawer holding only dust
branches.cn: 空抽屉里只有一层灰

branches.en: a hand patting a pocket with no keys in it
branches.cn: 手拍口袋，里面没有钥匙

branches.en: a quarrel over something too small to name
branches.cn: 为一件小得叫不出名字的事争吵

branches.en: a scoreboard still blank after the first half
branches.cn: 半场过后记分牌上仍是空白

branches.en: a team walking off with a zero beside its name
branches.cn: 球队离场，名字旁边是一个零

intro.en: The word joins an Old English negative for not one to the noun for thing, and English built its abstract noun and its dismissive compound on that base.
intro.cn: 这个词把古英语表示「一个也不」的否定词接到表示「东西」的名词上，英语又在这个底座上造出抽象名词和表示轻蔑的复合词。

latinIntro.en: Nothing has no reliable Latin cognate; Latin nihil is built from ne and hilum, not a whit, a different formation, so no Latin entry is listed.
latinIntro.cn: nothing 没有可靠的拉丁同族词；拉丁语用「nihil」表示「无」，它由「ne」与「hilum」（一点点）构成，构词方式不同，因此不列拉丁词条。

definition_zh: 注意到；察觉；通知；告知；告示；通告；短评
definition_en: to become aware of something; also a formal statement that tells people something, a written public sign, and a short review in a newspaper
core_image: 眼睛忽然停在某处细小的地方，心里咯噔一下：我看见了
scene: 雨后的公交站牌下，等车的人无意间抬头，视线落在路对面那件深色外套上。She noticed a small stain on the man's collar as he stood in line.
sceneCN: 这里 notice 是「注意到、察觉」（第 1 个义项：用眼睛或心思捕捉到某个细节）；句意为排队时她注意到前面那人衣领上有一小块污渍。图中可辨识物件：候车的人、路牌、雨后的地面。

collocations.zh: 在很短的通知时间内；临时

derivatives.zh: 由动词 notice 加后缀 -able 构成，义为「容易被注意到的；明显的」
由否定前缀 un- 加 noticed 构成，义为「未被注意到的」
由 noticeable 加后缀 -ly 构成，义为「明显地」

senses.title: To become aware of something
senses.definition: to see, hear or realize something, often without deliberately looking for it
senses.definitionCN: 看见、听见或意识到某事，往往并非刻意寻找
senses.example: She noticed a small stain on his collar.
senses.exampleCN: 她注意到他衣领上有一小块污渍。
senses.why: The Latin source notitia names the state of something being known, so this verb starts from a fact entering your mind rather than from a deliberate search.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 notitia 指「被知道的状态」，所以这个动词的起点是某个事实自己进了心里，而不是刻意去找。

senses.title: A formal statement that tells someone something
senses.definition: an official or formal message or warning given to a person who must act on it
senses.definitionCN: 正式或官方地告知某人的消息、警告，收信人往往要据此行动
senses.example: The tenant received notice that the rent would rise in spring.
senses.exampleCN: 租客收到了房租将在春天上涨的通知。
senses.why: Once notitia means a piece of knowledge, it can also mean handing that knowledge to someone who must respond, which is why the noun turns official.
senses.whyCN: notitia 既然能指「一条已知的消息」，也就能指把这条消息交给需要作出回应的人，于是这个名词带上了正式、官方的色彩。

senses.title: A written sign giving public information
senses.definition: a piece of paper or a sign placed in a public spot to tell people something
senses.definitionCN: 张贴在公共场所、用来告知信息的纸片或牌子
senses.example: A notice on the door said the library would close early.
senses.exampleCN: 门上的一张告示说图书馆会提前关门。
senses.why: A written notice is knowledge fixed on paper, so the same word moves from what is told to what is posted for everyone to read.
senses.whyCN: 书面告示就是把「已知的消息」固定在纸上，同一个词便从「被告知的事」转到「贴出来给所有人看的东西」。

senses.title: A short review of a performance or book
senses.definition: a short newspaper article that judges a play, film or book
senses.definitionCN: 报刊上评价戏剧、电影或书籍的短文
senses.example: The young actor got a favourable notice in the morning paper.
senses.exampleCN: 这位年轻演员在晨报上得到了一篇好评。
senses.why: Nineteenth-century papers printed such reviews beside announcements, so a word for an announcement came to name a printed judgement of a performance as well.
senses.whyCN: 十九世纪的报纸把剧评和各类公告排在一起，于是原本表示「通告」的词也用来指印在报上的演出评价。

intro.en: Notice comes from a Latin noun for being known, travelled through French, and keeps both the act of seeing and the official statement in modern English.
intro.cn: notice 源自拉丁语中表示「被知晓」的名词，经法语传入英语，至今同时保留「看见」与「正式告知」两条线索。

items.en: The verb noscere meant to get to know or to recognise, and it is the root behind a whole family of words about knowledge.
items.cn: 动词 noscere 意为认识、认出，是整族「知识」词汇共同的根。

items.en: Notitia named the state of being known, and could also mean a piece of information or an acquaintance.
items.cn: notitia 指「被知道的状态」，也可指一则消息或一位相识的人。

items.en: Old French kept notice for information, knowledge and a warning, and passed the word into English after the Norman period.
items.cn: 古法语保留 notice 一词，表示消息、知识与警告，并在诺曼时期之后把它传入英语。

items.en: In Middle English the word covered both what a person came to know and the formal warning that told people what to do.
items.cn: 在中古英语里，这个词既指一个人得知的事，也指告诉人们该怎么做的正式警告。

items.en: Modern English adds the public written sign and the newspaper review, while the verb stays close to simply seeing something.
items.cn: 现代英语又添上公共场所的书面告示与报刊短评，而动词仍旧贴近「看见了什么」这一层。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same Latin root for knowing; the near-meaning group gathers verbs for perceiving.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁「知道」词根上的词；近义组收表示察觉的动词。

entries.definition: An idea or belief held in the mind.
entries.definitionCN: 头脑中持有的一种想法或看法。

entries.definition: Important or unusual enough to deserve attention.
entries.definitionCN: 重要或不寻常到值得留意的。

entries.definition: A system of written signs used in music or mathematics.
entries.definitionCN: 音乐或数学中使用的一套书写符号。

entries.definition: The state of being widely known for something bad.
entries.definitionCN: 因坏事而广为人知的状态。

entries.definition: To become aware of something through the senses.
entries.definitionCN: 通过感官察觉到某事物。

entries.definition: To watch something carefully and take in the details.
entries.definitionCN: 仔细观察并留意细节。

entries.definition: To find something that is hidden or easy to miss.
entries.definitionCN: 发现隐藏或容易漏掉的事物。

entries.definition: To make out something that is not obvious.
entries.definitionCN: 辨认出并不明显的事物。

normalIntro.en: The word is built on a Latin root for knowing, and its two halves, seeing and telling, both grow from the same idea of something becoming known.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词长在表示「知道」的拉丁词根上，它的两半——看见与告知——都出自「某事被知道」这同一个念头。

normal.en: Noscere in Latin means to get to know, so notice is what happens when something becomes known to your eyes.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 noscere 意为认识，所以 notice 就是某样东西被你的眼睛知道的那一刻。

normal.en: Notice entered English first as a noun from notitia; the verb came later by using the noun as an action.
normal.cn: notice 先以名词身份从 notitia 进入英语，动词是后来把这个名词当动作来用。

normal.en: Noticeable adds -able to notice, meaning able to be noticed, and the final e stays before the suffix.
normal.cn: noticeable 在 notice 后加 -able，意为「能被注意到的」，词尾的 e 在加后缀时保留。

normal.en: Notify is built differently: notus plus -ify, to make known, so it means telling someone officially rather than merely seeing.
normal.cn: notify 的构造不同：notus 加 -ify，意为「使被知道」，所以它指正式告知某人，而不只是看见。

normal.en: At short notice means with very little warning, because notice here is the time given before something happens.
normal.cn: at short notice 意为几乎没有提前告知，因为这里的 notice 指事情发生前留给你的那段时间。

abstract.en: A notice board holds many small facts pinned in place, each waiting for the one person who needs it.
abstract.cn: 布告栏上钉着许多小事，每一件都在等那个恰好需要它的人。

abstract.en: Seeing and telling are two ends of one thread: what you notice may later have to be announced to others.
abstract.cn: 看见与告知是同一条线的两端：你注意到的事，后来可能要告知别人。

abstract.en: A word that can mean a glance and a resignation letter shows how much weight lies in simply being told.
abstract.cn: 一个词既能指一瞥，又能指辞职信，说明「被告知」这件事本身有多重。

examples.en: She noticed a small stain on his collar.
examples.cn: 她注意到他衣领上有一小块污渍。

examples.en: The staff were given notice of the change in the rota.
examples.cn: 员工们收到了排班变更的通知。

examples.en: A handwritten notice was pinned beside the lift.
examples.cn: 电梯旁钉着一张手写的告示。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「诺替事」——答应替人办事，就得时时留意、件件告知；notice 既是留意，也是通知。

root: 一般认为来自拉丁语 notitia（被知道的状态），源于 noscere（认识），经古法语 notice 进入英语；同族词多与「知道、记号」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is something entering your awareness; from there the word splits into the private act of seeing and the public act of telling, with the posted sign and the printed review as its outward forms.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是某样东西进入你的意识；由此分出私下「看见」与公开「告知」两条路，张贴的告示与报刊短评则是它外在的形态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pair of eyes stopping on one small detail while the mind registers it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一双眼睛停在某个细小之处，心里记下了它。

branches.en: a glance that catches a stain on a collar
branches.cn: 一眼瞥见衣领上的污渍

branches.en: a fact moving from one mind to another
branches.cn: 一件事从一个人心里传到另一个人心里

branches.en: a sheet of paper pinned beside a door
branches.cn: 钉在门边的一张纸

branches.en: a letter that warns of a coming change
branches.cn: 预告即将变动的一封信

branches.en: a short column judging a new play
branches.cn: 评价一部新戏的短栏

intro.en: The word rests on a Latin verb for knowing and a Latin noun for being known, then passes through French without carrying an English prefix of its own.
intro.cn: 这个词立在表示「认识」的拉丁动词与表示「被知道」的拉丁名词上，经法语进入英语，本身不带英语前缀。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: to get to know, to recognise

derivatives.zh: 同一词根上的名词，义为「概念；想法」
同一词根上的形容词，义为「值得注意的」

definition_zh: 小说；长篇小说；新奇的；新颖的；新颁律令（罕用）
definition_en: a long written story about imaginary people and events; also new and unlike anything seen before
core_image: 一本摊开的长篇手稿，纸页很新，故事却是从未有人讲过的
scene: 清晨的旧书店里，店主把一本厚厚的故事书摆到最显眼的位置。She borrowed a novel from the library and read it in two nights.
sceneCN: 这里是「小说、长篇小说」（第 1 个义项：虚构的长篇故事）；句意为她从图书馆借了一本小说，两个晚上就读完了。场景里可辨的物件：旧书架、厚书、昏黄的灯。

derivatives.zh: 由 novel 加表示「从事某事的人」的后缀 -ist 构成，义为「小说家」
由 novel 加名词后缀 -ty 构成，义为「新奇；新鲜事」
由 novelist 加 -ic 构成，义为「小说式的；具有小说特点的」

senses.title: A long work of fiction
senses.definition: a long written story in which the events and characters are imagined rather than real
senses.definitionCN: 篇幅较长、情节与人物皆为虚构的书面故事
senses.example: Her first novel was published when she was twenty.
senses.exampleCN: 她的第一部小说在二十岁时出版。
senses.why: The noun entered English from Italian novella, a short tale, and later grew to mean a full-length invented story.
senses.whyCN: 名词义经意大利语 novella（短篇故事）进入英语，后来指篇幅完整的虚构故事；它和形容词「新」共用同一拉丁词根，因为故事讲的正是没见过的事。

senses.title: New and unlike what came before
senses.definition: new, original and not seen or done before
senses.definitionCN: 新的、独创的、此前未曾见过或做过的
senses.example: They proposed a novel solution to the traffic problem.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为交通问题提出了一个新奇的解决办法。
senses.why: The adjective goes back to Latin novellus, a small form of novus meaning new, so freshness is the oldest layer of the word.
senses.whyCN: 形容词可追到拉丁语 novellus，它是 novus（新的）的小称形式，所以「新鲜」才是这个词最古老的一层意思。

senses.title: A newly issued decree
senses.definition: a new decree or supplementary constitution, especially in civil law
senses.definitionCN: 尤指民法中新增的法令或补充律令，现代英语已罕用
senses.example: The old code was amended by a series of novels.
senses.exampleCN: 旧法典经一系列新颁律令得到修订。
senses.why: In civil law the plural novels named the new constitutions added after the main code, keeping the bare sense of something newly issued.
senses.whyCN: 在民法传统里，复数形式 novels 指编入主法典之后的新律令，保留了「新颁之物」的字面意思；这个义项今天基本只出现在法律史里。

intro.en: Novel runs on two rails from the same Latin root: an adjective for what is new, and a noun for an invented story that was itself a novelty.
intro.cn: novel 沿着同一拉丁词根分出两条路：形容词指「新的」，名词指虚构故事，而这类故事在当时本身就是新鲜事物。

items.en: Novus meant new, fresh or recent, and it stands behind a large family of words about novelty.
items.cn: novus 意为新的、新鲜的、刚出现的，是表示「新」的一大族词的共同词根。

items.en: Novellus was a diminutive of novus, literally newish or young, and it passed into several Romance languages.
items.cn: novellus 是 novus 的小称，字面意思是「较新的、年轻的」，它进入了多种罗曼语。

items.en: Old French novel meant new or fresh, and English took the adjective with that plain sense.
items.cn: 古法语 novel 意为新的、新鲜的，英语借入的形容词就带着这层朴素的意思。

items.en: Italian novella named a short tale, and through French nouvelle it gave English the noun for a story.
items.cn: 意大利语 novella 指短篇故事，经法语 nouvelle 传给英语，成为表示「故事」的名词。

items.en: Modern English keeps the adjective novel for anything strikingly new and the noun novel for a full-length fictional work.
items.cn: 现代英语保留形容词 novel 指「格外新的」，名词 novel 则指篇幅完整的虚构作品。

note.en: The look-alike group collects relatives on the same Latin root; the near-meaning group collects words for stories and for newness.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁词根上的同族词，近义组收表示故事与「新」的词。

entries.definition: A short novel or a long short story.
entries.definitionCN: 篇幅较短的小说，或较长的短篇故事。

entries.definition: The quality of being new, or a small new thing.
entries.definitionCN: 新奇的性质，或新奇的小物件。

entries.definition: A person who writes novels.
entries.definitionCN: 写小说的人；小说家。

entries.definition: To introduce new ideas or methods.
entries.definitionCN: 引入新想法或新方法。

entries.definition: A person who is new to an activity or field.
entries.definitionCN: 刚接触某项活动或领域的新手。

entries.definition: Stories and characters that are invented rather than real.
entries.definitionCN: 虚构的故事与人物，而非真人真事。

entries.definition: An account of events, whether real or imagined.
entries.definitionCN: 对事件的叙述，真实的或想象的。

entries.definition: New in design and not copied from anything else.
entries.definitionCN: 设计上新的，不是照搬别处的。

entries.definition: Recently made, arrived or thought of, and therefore new.
entries.definitionCN: 刚做出、刚到达或刚想到的，因而显得新。

normalIntro.en: The root nov means new, and from it grow the novel, the novelty and the person who writes novels.
normalIntro.cn: 词根 nov 表示「新」，小说、新奇与写小说的人都从它长出来。

normal.en: The Latin root nov means new, which is why a novel idea is simply a new idea.
normal.cn: 拉丁词根 nov 表示「新」，所以 a novel idea 就是一个新想法。

normal.en: Novelty adds -ty to the same stem and turns new into a noun: the state of being new.
normal.cn: novelty 在同一词干后加 -ty，把「新」变成名词，指「新奇」这种状态。

normal.en: Novelist adds -ist, the suffix for a person, so it names the one who writes a novel.
normal.cn: novelist 加的是表示人的后缀 -ist，因此指写小说的人。

normal.en: Italian novella, a short tale, is the ancestor of the noun, which is why the two senses look unrelated.
normal.cn: 意大利语 novella 意为短篇故事，是名词义的祖先，所以两个义项看起来像是毫无关系。

normal.en: The adjective takes more novel and most novel, not noveler, because it is a longer adjective.
normal.cn: 形容词的比较级说 more novel、most novel，而不是 noveler，因为它属于较长的形容词。

abstract.en: A story and a new thing share one root because every story is, in a small way, something that did not exist before.
abstract.cn: 故事和新事物共用一个词根，因为每个故事在某种意义上都是过去不存在的东西。

abstract.en: Reading a novel means being handed a world that someone invented, so freshness lives inside the fictional sense too.
abstract.cn: 读一本小说，就是接过一个别人造出来的世界，所以「新」也活在虚构的那个义项里。

abstract.en: The word keeps two doors open: one leads to invention and one to novelty, and both open on the same Latin room.
abstract.cn: 这个词留着两扇门：一扇通向虚构，一扇通向新奇，而它们开在同一间拉丁语的屋子里。

examples.en: Her first novel was published when she was twenty.
examples.cn: 她的第一部小说在二十岁时出版。

examples.en: They proposed a novel solution to the traffic problem.
examples.cn: 他们为交通问题提出了一个新奇的解决办法。

examples.en: He writes novels about life in small mountain villages.
examples.cn: 他写关于山区小村生活的小说。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「闹窝」——书里的故事闹成一窝，让人读到深夜；记住 novel 是小说。

root: 拉丁语 novus（新的）→ 小称 novellus（较新的）→ 形容词经古法语 novel 进入英语；名词义经意大利语 novella（短篇故事）与法语 nouvelle 而来。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the Latin root for new; one branch names an invented long story, another describes anything strikingly fresh, and a third survives only in legal history.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是拉丁语表示「新」的词根；一条分支指虚构的长篇故事，一条形容格外新鲜的事物，第三条只留在法律史里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a freshly written manuscript holding a story that nobody has told before.
core.cn: 核心意象：一叠刚写就的手稿，里面装着无人讲过的故事。

branches.cn: 床头摊开的一本厚书

branches.en: a reader refusing to close the last page
branches.cn: 读者舍不得合上最后一页

branches.en: a designer sketching a route no map has shown
branches.cn: 设计师画出一条地图上没有的路线

branches.en: a crowd hearing a proposal that breaks the old pattern
branches.cn: 众人听到一个打破旧套的方案

branches.en: a clerk copying a new decree into the law book
branches.cn: 书记员把新律令抄进法典

intro.en: The word rests on a Latin root for new, its adjective and its small form, plus two English suffixes that build the writer and the quality.

latinIntro.en: Latin novus and its small form novellus supply the whole family, from the adjective novel to the noun novelty.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 novus 及其小称 novellus 支撑起整族词，从形容词 novel 到名词 novelty。

definition_zh: 现今；如今；当今；眼下
definition_en: at the present time, especially when the present is set against the past
core_image: 一张旧照片和一张新照片并排摆着，同一条街已经换了模样
scene: 老人在巷口翻出旧相片，指着同一处街角说当年的店铺早就不在了。Nowadays the street is full of coffee shops instead of grocery stores.
sceneCN: 这里是「现今、如今」（第 1 个义项：指当下的时间）；句意为如今这条街上全是咖啡馆，不再是杂货店。旧照与新街并置，让这个词的时间感更清楚。

derivatives.zh: 由 now 与 day 缩合而来的形容词，多见于旧用法，义为「现今的」
nowadays 的构词基干之一，源自古英语 nu，义为「现在」

senses.title: At the present time
senses.definition: at the present time, in the period we are living in now
senses.definitionCN: 在我们正生活的当下这个时期
senses.example: Nowadays most people carry a phone everywhere.
senses.exampleCN: 如今大多数人走到哪里都带着手机。
senses.why: The phrase behind the word literally meant now on days, so its first job is simply to place an action in the present.
senses.whyCN: 这个词背后的短语字面上就是「如今在这些日子里」，所以它最基本的工作是把动作安放在当下。

senses.title: The present seen against the past
senses.definition: used to point out how things differ between the present and an earlier time
senses.definitionCN: 用来指出现在与从前之间的差别
senses.example: Nowadays we order food online, but my grandmother still walks to the market.
senses.exampleCN: 如今我们在网上点菜，可我祖母还是走去菜市场。
senses.why: Because the phrase grew out of a comparison between days, the word naturally carries a before-and-after frame.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语本就诞生于「日子与日子」的对照，所以这个词天然带着「前后之别」的框架。

senses.title: Of the present period, placed before a noun
senses.titleCN: 时下的；当今的（口语用法）
senses.definition: placed before a noun in informal speech to mean belonging to the present period
senses.definitionCN: 口语中放在名词前，表示属于当下这个时期的
senses.example: Nowadays children learn to swipe a screen before they learn to write.
senses.exampleCN: 现在的孩子先学会滑屏幕，再学会写字。
senses.why: Once the adverb is felt as a label for the current era, speakers begin to use it as a modifier of the people and things that belong to that era.
senses.whyCN: 当这个副词被当成「当下时代」的标签，说话人就开始把它放到名词前，修饰属于这个时代的人与物。

intro.en: Nowadays began as a spoken phrase rather than a single word: now on days, which English later squeezed into one adverb.
intro.cn: nowadays 起初是一个口语短语而不是单词：now on days，后来英语把它压缩成一个副词。

items.en: The two halves are old: nu meant now, and dæg meant day.
items.cn: 两半都很古老：nu 意为「现在」，dæg 意为「日子」。

items.en: Middle English joined them in the phrase now a dayes, literally now on days, with a as a worn-down form of on.
items.cn: 中古英语把它们连成 now a dayes，字面是「如今在这些日子里」，其中的 a 是 on 的弱化形式。

items.en: By the sixteenth century the phrase was written as one word, and the old preposition had disappeared from hearing.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，这个短语被写成一个词，旧的介词在听感上已经消失。

items.en: Dictionaries of the eighteenth century list it as a settled adverb of present time.
items.cn: 十八世纪的词典已把它收作表示现在时间的固定副词。

items.en: Modern English uses it mainly in writing and in contrastive statements about how things have changed.
items.cn: 现代英语主要在书面语里、以及在说明事物如何变化的今昔对比句中使用。

note.en: The look-alike group collects short time words built from the same demonstrative parts; the near-meaning group collects other ways of saying now.
note.cn: 形近组收由同一批指示词构成的短小时间词，近义组收其他表示「现在」的说法。

entries.definitionCN: 此刻或现在。

entries.definition: On this present day.
entries.definitionCN: 在今天这一天。

entries.definition: In or to no place.
entries.definitionCN: 不在任何地方；无处。

entries.definition: Sometimes, but not often.

entries.definitionCN: 目前，常见于中性或正式书面语。

entries.definition: In the present period, especially in speech.
entries.definitionCN: 在当前这段时期，多用于口语。

entries.definition: At this time, or soon, depending on the sentence.
entries.definitionCN: 现时，或视句子指「不久」。

normalIntro.en: Split the word into now, a and dayes and it says now on these days, which is simply the present.
normalIntro.cn: 把词拆成 now、a、dayes 三段，意思就是「在这些日子里」，也就是现在。

normal.en: Nowadays hides the words now and day inside it, and together they mean now on these days.
normal.cn: nowadays 里藏着 now 与 day，合起来就是「如今在这些日子里」。

normal.en: The a in the middle is a worn-down on, so the phrase once read as now on days.
normal.cn: 中间那个 a 是弱化掉的 on，所以这个短语原本读作 now on days。

normal.en: The final -s is the plural of day, which is why the word points to a stretch of days rather than one date.
normal.cn: 末尾的 -s 是 day 的复数，所以这个词指的是一段日子，而不是某一天。

normal.en: Nowadays is an adverb, so in careful writing it modifies a whole clause rather than standing before a noun.
normal.cn: nowadays 是副词，在严谨的写作里它修饰整个句子，而不是站在名词前面。

normal.en: Its closest short synonym in speech is these days, which carries the same contrast with the past.
normal.cn: 口语里它最贴近的短说法是 these days，同样带着与过去对照的意味。

abstract.en: The word is a fossil of a phrase: a whole remark about days was squeezed until it fit into one slot.
abstract.cn: 这个词是一个短语的化石：一句关于日子的话被压缩到只占一个位置。

abstract.en: Hearing nowadays always implies a before, because a contrast with the past is built into its bones.
abstract.cn: 听到 nowadays 总会预设一个「从前」，因为与过去的对照已经长在它的骨架里。

abstract.en: It measures time the way a photograph does: it does not give the clock, only the fact that the picture has changed.
abstract.cn: 它衡量时间的方式像一张照片：它不报钟点，只说明画面已经变了。

definition_zh: 数；数字；号码；数量；编号；总计
definition_en: a word or symbol used for counting, a label that identifies something, an amount or total, and the act of counting a group
core_image: 一列整齐的算珠，每一颗都占着一个可以数出来的位置
scene: 深夜的急诊室门口，护士低头核对登记本，把票上的号码念了出来。The clerk read the number on the ticket and called the next patient in.
sceneCN: 这里的 number 是「号码」（第 2 个义项：用来识别身份的编号）；句意为工作人员读出票上的号码，叫下一位病人进来。图中可辨识物件：登记本、排号票、叫号屏。

derivatives.zh: 由 number 加表示「没有」的后缀 -less 构成，义为「数不清的；无数的」
由 number 加 -ing 构成，义为「编号；编号方式」
与拉丁词根 numerus（数）同源，加 -ous 后义为「众多的」

senses.title: A word or symbol used for counting
senses.definition: a word or written sign, such as three or seven, used to count things or to show an amount
senses.definitionCN: 用来计数或表示数量的词或书写符号，例如「三」或「七」
senses.example: Write the number seven at the top of the page.
senses.exampleCN: 把数字七写在页面顶端。
senses.why: The Latin noun numerus named a count, and English kept the idea of a unit you can point at, so the sign for a count and the count itself share one name.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁名词 numerus 指「数目」，英语保留了「可以被指认的一个计数单位」这个想法，因此表示数目的符号与数目本身共用同一个词。

senses.title: A label that identifies a person or thing
senses.definition: a set of figures or a single figure printed on something so that it can be told apart from others
senses.definitionCN: 印在物品上的一组数字或一个数字，用来把它与别的同类区分开
senses.example: Her phone number changed after she moved.
senses.exampleCN: 搬家之后她的电话号码变了。
senses.why: Once a figure marks a position in a list, it can also mark identity, because a house, a phone or a ticket is known by the figure printed on it.
senses.whyCN: 数字一旦标出某物在名单中的位置，也就能标出身份，因为房子、电话或票据正是靠印在上面的数字被人认出的。

senses.title: The total amount of a group
senses.definition: the total count of people or things, especially when it is measured or compared with another total
senses.definitionCN: 人或物的总数，尤指被计量或与另一个总数作比较时
senses.example: The number of visitors doubled this summer.
senses.exampleCN: 今年夏天游客数量翻了一倍。
senses.why: Counting a whole group produces one total, so English let the word for a count stand for the size of the group itself.
senses.whyCN: 把一整群数完会得到一个总数，于是英语让表示计数的词直接指这一群的大小。

senses.title: One item in a numbered series
senses.definition: a single item in a numbered series, such as a song in a show or an issue of a magazine, named by its position
senses.definitionCN: 按编号排列的序列中的一项，如演出中的一首歌或杂志的一期，用它的位置来称呼
senses.example: She sang the closing number of the show.
senses.exampleCN: 她唱了演出的压轴曲目。
senses.why: A position in a list turns into a name for whatever sits in that position, so performers speak of the next number without naming the song.
senses.whyCN: 名单上的一个位置会变成占据那个位置的事物的名字，所以演员会说「下一号节目」，而不必点出歌名。

senses.title: To amount to a total
senses.definition: to add up to a particular total, or to count a group and find how many there are
senses.definitionCN: 加起来达到某个总数，或把一群数一遍以得出有多少
senses.example: The crowd numbered more than a thousand.
senses.exampleCN: 人群总数超过了一千人。
senses.why: When a count is applied to a whole group, the noun turns into a verb: you number the group and arrive at its total.
senses.whyCN: 当「数」这个动作落到一整群上，名词就转成动词：你把这群数一遍，就得到它的总数。

intro.en: Number comes from Latin numerus, a word for a count, which reached English through Old French and kept both the thing counted and the act of counting.
intro.cn: number 来自拉丁语 numerus，本义是「数目」，经古法语进入英语，同时保留了「被数的东西」和「数这个动作」两重意思。

items.en: Numerus meant a number, a count or a group counted together, and it was the everyday word for arithmetic quantities.
items.cn: numerus 指数目、计数或一起数出的一群，是表示算术数量的常用词。

items.en: The verb numerare meant to count or to enumerate, and it supplied the action behind the English noun.
items.cn: 动词 numerare 意为数、逐一清点，为英语名词提供了「数」这个动作。

items.en: Old French shortened the Latin word to nombre, which named both a figure and a total; English borrowed this form rather than the Latin one.
items.cn: 古法语把拉丁词缩短为 nombre，既指数字也指总数；英语借的是这个形式，而不是拉丁原形。

items.en: Middle English wrote the borrowed word as noumbre or nombre and used it for figures, totals and the numbering of things in order.
items.cn: 中古英语把借来的词写作 noumbre 或 nombre，用来指数目、总数以及按顺序编号。

items.en: Modern English fixed the spelling as number and extended it to phone numbers, house numbers, magazine issues and musical items.
items.cn: 现代英语把拼写固定为 number，并把词义扩展到电话号码、门牌号、杂志期号与演出曲目。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on the same Latin stem; the near-meaning group collects other words for figures, amounts and totals.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁词干上的词；近义组收其他表示数字、数量与总数的词。

entries.definition: A written sign or word that stands for a number.
entries.definitionCN: 代表一个数的书写符号或词。

entries.definition: Existing in large numbers; very many.
entries.definitionCN: 数量很多的；众多的。

entries.definition: To name things one by one, as if counting them.
entries.definitionCN: 逐一列举，如同清点。

entries.definition: Able to understand and work with numbers.
entries.definitionCN: 会读会算的；有计算能力的。

entries.definition: One of the written signs from zero to nine used to build numbers.
entries.definitionCN: 从零到九的书写符号之一，用来组成数字。

entries.definition: A written symbol for a number, or an amount expressed in numbers.
entries.definitionCN: 数字符号，或用数字表示的数额。

entries.definition: An amount or number of something, often measured.
entries.definitionCN: 某物的数量，常指可计量的量。

entries.definition: The whole amount reached when everything is added together.
entries.definitionCN: 把所有部分加在一起得到的全部数额。

normalIntro.en: The word rests on a Latin noun of counting, and its family keeps returning to signs, totals and the act of naming things in order.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在表示计数的拉丁名词上，同族词反复回到符号、总数以及按顺序点名的动作。

normal.en: Numerus in Latin means a count, so number begins as something you can point at before it becomes an abstract idea.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 numerus 意为数目，所以 number 起初是能用手指数出来的东西，之后才变成抽象概念。

normal.en: Numeral and numerous share the same stem: one names the sign, the other says how many there are.
normal.cn: numeral 与 numerous 共用同一词干：一个指符号，另一个说数量有多少。

normal.en: Enumerate adds en- and -ate to the same stem, literally counting items out one at a time.
normal.cn: enumerate 在同一词干前加 en-、后加 -ate，字面就是一项一项数出来。

normal.en: A phone number or a house number is a count turned into an identity label.
normal.cn: 电话号码或门牌号，是被转成身份标签的计数。

normal.en: In the phrase a number of, the word stops naming a figure and starts meaning a group of things.
normal.cn: 在 a number of 这个词组里，它不再指一个数字，而开始表示一群事物。

abstract.en: A number is a promise that unlike things can still be compared, because it puts them on one scale.
abstract.cn: 数字是一种承诺：彼此不同的事物也能比较，因为它把它们放在同一把尺子上。

abstract.en: That one word covers symbol, total and label shows how counting turns the world into something English can manage.
abstract.cn: 一个词同时覆盖符号、总数与标签，说明计数把世界变成了英语可以打理的东西。

abstract.en: Every number is a position on an endless line, which is why a figure can also name a place in a queue.
abstract.cn: 每个数都是无尽直线上的一个位置，所以一个数字也能指队列中的某个位次。

examples.en: The number of rainy days fell sharply this year.
examples.cn: 今年雨天的数量大幅下降。

examples.en: Please write your membership number on the form.
examples.cn: 请在表格上写下你的会员编号。

examples.en: The volunteers numbered over forty at the end of the day.

definition_zh: 服从；听从；遵守；遵从
definition_en: to do what a person, a rule or a force tells you to do, or to act in the way it requires
core_image: 一只脚已经迈出去，又被收回到别人指定的位置上
scene: 祠堂的院子里，长辈把香递到年轻人手里，只说了该站的位置，没有再解释。The young man obeyed and stepped back two paces without a word.
sceneCN: 这里 obeyed 是「服从、听从」（第 1 个义项：按有威权的人的要求行动）；句意为年轻人照做，一言不发地退后两步。图中可辨识物件：祠堂院子、递出的香、后退的脚步。

senses.title: Doing what a person in authority asks
senses.definition: to do what someone with authority over you tells you to do, even when you would rather not
senses.definitionCN: 按有权威的人的要求去做，哪怕自己并不情愿
senses.example: The soldiers obeyed every order without question.
senses.exampleCN: 士兵们毫无质疑地服从每一道命令。
senses.why: Latin oboedire was built from ob-, toward, and audire, to hear; obey therefore begins as leaning your ear toward a voice and letting it decide your next move.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 oboedire 由 ob-（朝向）加 audire（听）构成，所以 obey 的起点是把耳朵朝向一个声音，并让它决定你下一步怎么走。

senses.title: Acting according to a rule or law
senses.definition: to act in the way that a law, rule or set of instructions requires
senses.definitionCN: 按照法律、规则或一套指示所要求的方式行事
senses.example: Every driver must obey the speed limit on this road.
senses.exampleCN: 每位司机在这条路上都必须遵守限速。
senses.why: Once the voice that must be heard belongs to a written rule instead of a person, the same yielding turns into keeping the law, which is why obey fits a captain and a statute alike.
senses.whyCN: 当那个必须听从的声音从一个人变成一条写下来的规则，同样的「让位」就变成守法；所以 obey 既能跟长官，也能跟法条。

senses.title: Following what an inner feeling urges
senses.definition: to act on what a feeling, instinct or urge tells you to do
senses.definitionCN: 按照某种感觉、本能或冲动的要求行动
senses.example: She obeyed her instincts and turned back before the bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 她听从直觉，在桥前折了回来。
senses.why: The one who gives the order can also sit inside you, so the verb stretches from an outer voice to an urge that feels like a command.
senses.whyCN: 下命令的人也可以坐在你身体里，于是这个动词从外面的声音延伸到一种像命令一样的冲动。

senses.title: Of a thing, answering a control
senses.definition: of a machine, ship or system, to move or work in the way a control or force directs it
senses.definitionCN: 指机器、船只或系统按操控或外力的方向运转
senses.example: The old boat obeyed the helm even in rough water.
senses.exampleCN: 这条旧船即使在浪里也随舵转向。
senses.why: A ship that answers the wheel is described as if it heard a command, which is how a word about human listening comes to describe machines that respond smoothly.
senses.whyCN: 一艘随舵转向的船，被说成像听见了命令；一个本来讲人「听」的词，就这样用来描述机器顺滑的响应。

intro.en: Obey travels from Latin through French; its Latin core joins a prefix meaning toward to a verb meaning hear, so the word begins with listening.
intro.cn: obey 经法语来自拉丁语，其拉丁核心是「朝向」的前缀加「听」的动词，所以这个词从「听」开始。

items.en: Audire meant to hear, and it supplied the sense of hearing that still hides inside this word.
items.cn: audire 意为听见，为这个词提供了藏在内部的「听」这一层意思。

items.en: Oboedire joined ob-, toward, with audire, so it meant to listen to and comply with a person who had the right to be heard.
items.cn: oboedire 把表示朝向的 ob- 与 audire 合在一起，意为听从、顺从一个有权被听见的人。

items.en: Old French obeir kept the sense of submitting to a person and passed the verb into English after the Norman period.
items.cn: 古法语 obeir 保留「顺从某人」的意思，在诺曼时期之后把动词传入英语。

items.en: Middle English obeien widened from obeying a person to obeying a rule, an order or a promise.
items.cn: 中古英语的 obeien 从服从一个人，扩展到遵守规则、命令或承诺。

items.en: Modern English also lets instincts, limbs and machines obey, while obedience and disobey keep the family together.
items.cn: 现代英语还让本能、肢体和机器也「服从」；obedience 与 disobey 把这个词族拢在一起。

normal.en: Oboedire joins ob-, toward, and audire, to hear, so to obey is first of all to turn your ear toward a voice.

normal.en: The opposite is disobey, built with the negative prefix dis-, and the noun behind it is disobedience.

normal.en: Obedient keeps the same Latin stem but adds -ent, the ending of an adjective, so the word becomes a quality of the person.
normal.cn: obedient 保留同一拉丁词干，加上形容词词尾 -ent，于是变成人的一种性质。

normal.en: Obedience is the noun, ending in -ence, and it names the state of being willing to listen.
normal.cn: 名词 obedience 以 -ence 收尾，指愿意倾听的那种状态。

normal.en: Obey often takes orders, rules or the law as its object, because what it follows is whatever has the right to be heard.

senses.example: A small object rolled under the table and stopped at her feet.
senses.exampleCN: 一个小东西滚到桌下，停在她脚边。
senses.why: Latin objectum names what has been thrown before the eyes, so the physical thing is the first thing this word ever pointed at.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 objectum 指「被抛到眼前的东西」，所以能看见的实物是这个词最初指向的对象。

senses.title: The focus of attention or feeling
senses.definition: a person or thing toward which attention, interest or a feeling is directed
senses.definitionCN: 注意力、兴趣或情感所指向的人或物
senses.example: The old house became the object of every photographer's attention.
senses.exampleCN: 那座老房子成了每个摄影师关注的对象。
senses.why: Once something is thrown before the mind, it can hold the mind there; the physical thing turns into whatever attention is aimed at.
senses.whyCN: 一样东西既然被抛到心里，就能把心思留住；实物于是转成「注意力瞄准的那个东西」。

senses.title: An aim that a plan is meant to reach
senses.definition: the aim that a plan or an action is meant to achieve
senses.definitionCN: 计划或行动想要达到的那一点
senses.example: The committee met with the object of cutting waiting times.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会开会，目的是缩短等候时间。
senses.why: An aim is also something placed in front of you to move toward, so the word shifts from what is looked at to what is worked for.
senses.whyCN: 目标也是放在你前方、要你走过去的东西，于是词义从「被看着的物」转到「为之努力的终点」。

senses.title: The noun that receives a verb's action
senses.definition: in grammar, the noun or pronoun that the action of a verb is done to
senses.definitionCN: 语法上，承受动词动作的名词或代词
senses.example: In the sentence she wrote the letter, the noun letter is the object.
senses.exampleCN: 在「她写了那封信」这句话里，名词 letter 是宾语。
senses.why: Grammar borrowed the word because the object is the thing placed before the verb's action, receiving what is done to it.
senses.whyCN: 语法借用这个词，因为宾语正是被放到动词动作前面的东西，承受着被做的动作。

senses.title: To say that you disagree
senses.definition: to say that you do not agree with or approve of something
senses.definitionCN: 表示不同意或不赞成某事
senses.example: Several neighbours objected to the plan for a new car park.
senses.exampleCN: 好几位邻居反对新建停车场的方案。
senses.why: Latin obicere meant to throw something against someone, and an objection is a word thrown back at a proposal; the modern verb keeps that gesture of standing in the way.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 obicere 意为把东西朝某人扔过去，而反对就是把一句话扔回给一个提议；这个现代动词保留了「挡在前面」的动作。

intro.en: Object comes from Latin words for throwing something before or against; the same root splits into a noun for what is placed in view and a verb for speaking against it.
intro.cn: object 来自拉丁语「把东西抛到前面或对着扔」的说法；同一条词根分成两支，一支指摆在眼前的物，一支指对着说的反对。

items.en: Jacere meant to throw or to cast, and it lies under the -ject of many English words.
items.cn: jacere 意为投、掷，它藏在许多英语词的 -ject 一段里。

items.en: Obicere joined ob-, against or in front of, with jacere, so it meant to throw something in someone's way and also to throw a charge against a person.
items.cn: obicere 把表示对着、在前面的 ob- 与 jacere 合起来，意为把东西抛到某人面前，也指对某人提出责难。

items.en: Objectum, the thing thrown before the mind, came to name whatever is presented to thought, and later the target of a feeling or an aim.
items.cn: objectum 指被抛到心里的东西，用来指呈现在思想面前的一切，后来又指情感或目标所指向的靶子。

items.en: Old French took object as something perceived or opposed, and English borrowed it with both a noun and a verb in view.
items.cn: 古法语把这词用作「被感知之物」与「被反对之物」，英语借用时就同时看到了名词与动词两条路。

items.en: Modern English separates the two by stress: the noun keeps the first syllable strong, the verb moves the beat to the end, and grammar adds the sense of a verb's object.
items.cn: 现代英语用重音把两者分开：名词重音在前，动词重音挪到后面；语法上又添出「动词宾语」一义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same -ject stem from jacere; the near-meaning group gathers words for physical things and for speaking against something.
note.cn: 形近组收同一条 jacere 词干上的 -ject 词；近义组收表示实物与出言反对的词。

entries.definition: A statement or feeling of disagreement.
entries.definitionCN: 表示不同意的话或情绪；异议。

entries.definition: An aim, or something judged without personal feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 目标，或不受个人情感影响的。

entries.definition: A planned piece of work, or to throw something forward.
entries.definitionCN: 有计划的工作，或向前投射。

entries.definition: To put a liquid into the body with a needle.
entries.definitionCN: 用针把液体注入体内。

entries.definition: Any physical item or matter.
entries.definitionCN: 任何实物或东西。

entries.definition: One separate article in a list or a set.
entries.definitionCN: 列表或成套物品中单独的一件。

entries.definition: To say publicly that something is wrong.
entries.definitionCN: 公开表示某事不对。

entries.definition: To speak or act against a plan or an idea.
entries.definitionCN: 出言或行动反对某个计划或想法。

normalIntro.en: The word is built on a Latin verb for throwing, so every sense is some version of something placed in front of someone.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词长在表示「投掷」的拉丁动词上，所以每个义项都是「某样东西被放到某人面前」的某种变形。

normal.en: Jacere is Latin for throw, and the -ject in object, project and inject all comes from it.
normal.cn: jacere 在拉丁语里是投掷，object、project、inject 里的 -ject 都出自它。

normal.en: Object and objection share one root, but object names the thing in front of you while objection names the words thrown back.
normal.cn: object 与 objection 同根，但 object 指摆在眼前的物，objection 指扔回去的话。

normal.en: The noun takes the stress on the first syllable and the verb on the second, a split English made to keep the two jobs apart.
normal.cn: 名词把重音放在第一音节，动词放在第二音节，这是英语为了把两件事分开而做的切分。

normal.en: With the object of is a fixed phrase meaning with the aim of, because an object can be a goal.
normal.cn: with the object of 是固定说法，意为以……为目的，因为 object 可以是目标。

normal.en: Object to is followed by a noun or an -ing form, because the preposition to blocks the plain infinitive.
normal.cn: object to 后面接名词或动名词，因为介词 to 挡住了光秃秃的不定式。

abstract.en: Anything you can point at, anything you aim at, and anything you say against a plan are all, in this word, something placed in front of you.
abstract.cn: 你能指着的东西、你瞄准的东西、你对着计划说的话，在这个词里都是「被放到你面前的东西」。

abstract.en: The same root that throws a stone in someone's path also throws a thought before the mind.
abstract.cn: 同一条词根，既把石头扔到别人路上，也把一个念头扔到心里。

abstract.en: A word that names both a pebble and a protest shows how often disagreement begins with simply seeing something in the way.
abstract.cn: 一个既能指小石子、又能指抗议的词，说明不赞同常常始于「看见有东西挡在路上」。

examples.en: A small object rolled under the table and stopped at her feet.
examples.cn: 一个小东西滚到桌下，停在她脚边。

examples.en: Several neighbours objected to the plan for a new car park.
examples.cn: 好几位邻居反对新建停车场的方案。

examples.en: The committee met with the object of cutting waiting times.
examples.cn: 委员会开会，目的是缩短等候时间。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥不借它」——东西递到眼前偏说不借；object 既是眼前之物，也是出言反对。

root: 一般认为来自拉丁语 objectum（被抛到眼前之物），源于 obicere（对着投掷），由 ob-（对着）加 jacere（投掷）构成，经古法语 object 进入英语；名词与动词重音不同。

sensesIntro.en: The core is something thrown in front of you; from that one gesture come the physical thing, the target of attention, the aim in view, the grammatical receiver and the words spoken against a plan.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「被抛到你面前的东西」；同一个动作长出实物、注意力的靶子、眼前的目标、语法上的承受者，以及对着计划说出的话。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a solid thing held up before the eyes, and a hand raised to push it away.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件实物被托到眼前，随即有一只手把它推回去。

branches.en: a small thing rolling out of sight under a table
branches.cn: 小东西滚到桌下看不见的地方

branches.en: an old house drawing every camera in the street
branches.cn: 一座老房子引来街上所有的镜头

branches.en: a meeting called to shorten the wait at a stop
branches.cn: 为缩短站上等候时间而开的会

branches.en: the noun that takes what the verb does
branches.cn: 承受动词动作的那个名词

branches.en: neighbours standing up to speak against a plan
branches.cn: 邻居们站起来反对一个方案

intro.en: The word is Latin ob- plus jacere, and its English branch grows through endings that turn the stem into a noun of action and an adjective of judgement.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语的 ob- 加 jacere，它的英语分支靠后缀长成表示动作的名词与表示判断的形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin jacere, to throw, and its compounds obicere and objectum are the recorded source of this word, whose stem also underlies project and inject.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 jacere（投掷）及其复合词 obicere、objectum 是这个词语有记录的来源，它的词干也支撑着 project 与 inject。

definition_zh: 海洋；大洋；一片汪洋；大量
definition_en: the vast body of salt water that surrounds the continents and covers most of the earth
core_image: 一整片连成一体的咸水把陆地围在中间，望不到对岸，也数不清有多少层浪
scene: 地理课上，老师转动地球仪，指着连成一片的蓝色说，A single ocean can hold more water than all the land it surrounds.
sceneCN: 这里 ocean 指「地球上环绕陆地的巨大咸水体」（第 1 个义项：连成整体、覆盖大部分地表的咸水）；句意为：一个海洋能容纳的水量超过它周围全部陆地；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 海洋；大洋；（喻）大量、无边无际的一片
远洋的；海运的（如远洋货运、远洋航行）

derivatives.zh: 海洋的；辽阔如海的
海洋学
海洋学家
大型海洋水族馆
海滨地段；临海的
海洋研究；海洋学（较旧的说法）

senses.title: The world-encircling body of salt water
senses.titleCN: 覆盖地球大部分表面的连片咸水
senses.definition: the great body of salt water that surrounds the continents and covers most of the planet
senses.definitionCN: 环绕各大陆、覆盖地球大部分表面的巨大咸水体
senses.example: A single ocean can hold more water than all the land it surrounds.
senses.exampleCN: 一个海洋能容纳的水量超过它周围全部陆地。
senses.why: Greek Okeanos named the stream believed to run all the way around the world, so the word began as one continuous encircling water, not as a list of separate seas.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 Okeanos 原本指绕世界一周的大河，所以这个词从诞生起就是「一圈连着的咸水」，而非若干彼此分开的海。

senses.title: One of the named divisions
senses.titleCN: 五大洋中一个有名字的洋
senses.definition: one of the five large divisions of this water, such as the Pacific, Atlantic or Indian ocean
senses.definitionCN: 这片水域被划分出的五大洋之一，如太平洋、大西洋或印度洋
senses.example: The Atlantic ocean narrows toward its northern end.
senses.exampleCN: 大西洋在它的北端变窄。
senses.why: once geographers divided the single world water into named basins, the same word served both the whole and each part, and context decides which is meant.
senses.whyCN: 地理学家把这一整片世界水域划分成有名字的海盆之后，同一个词既指整体也指其中一部分，靠上下文决定所指。

senses.title: The water as opposed to the land
senses.definition: the open salt water thought of as a place distinct from land, especially in travel and trade
senses.definitionCN: 与陆地相对的开阔咸水，尤用于航行与贸易语境
senses.example: They spent three weeks on the ocean before sighting land.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在海上待了三个星期才看见陆地。
senses.why: a voyage needs two settings, land and water; the word supplies the second one, so 'on the ocean' simply means out on the salt water.
senses.whyCN: 一次远航需要两个场景：陆地与水面；这个词提供后者，因此「在海洋上」就是身处开阔咸水之中。

senses.title: A very large amount
senses.definition: an immense quantity of something, especially something abstract such as words or work
senses.definitionCN: 某事物数量极大，尤指话语、工作等抽象事物
senses.example: An ocean of paperwork awaited the new clerk.
senses.exampleCN: 海量的文书工作等着这位新职员。
senses.why: the figurative step is simple: the largest thing most speakers know becomes the measure of anything too big to count, so an ocean of forms is just too many forms.
senses.whyCN: 比喻的跳跃很简单：把说话人知道的最大之物拿来度量多到数不清的东西，因此「一整个海洋的表格」就是表格多到数不清。

senses.title: A boundless expanse
senses.definition: a vast unbroken stretch of something that seems to have no edge, such as sand or grass
senses.definitionCN: 沙、草等铺展到看不见边界的广阔一片
senses.example: An ocean of sand stretched from the road to the horizon.
senses.exampleCN: 一片沙海从路边一直铺到地平线。
senses.why: the eye reads any surface without a visible edge the way it reads water, so desert and prairie borrow the word for the same feeling of no boundary.
senses.whyCN: 人眼看到没有可见边界的表面时，读法与看水面一样，因此沙漠与草原借这个词表达同样的「无边」之感。

senses.title: A depth of feeling
senses.definition: an overwhelming quantity of a feeling that seems to swallow a person up
senses.definitionCN: 铺天盖地、仿佛把人吞没的情感
senses.example: She sank into an ocean of grief after the funeral.
senses.exampleCN: 葬礼之后，她沉入一片悲痛的汪洋。
senses.why: deep water is the standing image for what cannot be crossed or controlled, so grief and doubt are described as oceans, with the person inside them rather than beside them.
senses.whyCN: 深水一直是无从跨越、无法掌控的意象，因此悲伤与疑虑被说成海洋，而人是在其中，不在其旁。

senses.title: The ocean as a climate system
senses.definition: the salt water regarded as a system that stores heat, moves currents and regulates the atmosphere
senses.definitionCN: 把咸水视为储存热量、驱动洋流并调节大气的一个系统
senses.example: The ocean absorbs much of the heat trapped by greenhouse gases.
senses.exampleCN: 海洋吸收了温室气体截留的大部分热量。
senses.why: twentieth-century earth science turned the place into a mechanism: the same water that sails are built for is now studied as a store and pump of heat.
senses.whyCN: 20 世纪的地球科学把这个地点变成了机制：原本造船航行的同一片水，如今被当作热量的储库与泵来研究。

senses.title: The high seas in law
senses.definition: open water beyond any state's coastal jurisdiction, belonging to no single country
senses.definitionCN: 超出任何国家沿海管辖范围、不属任何一国所有的开阔水域
senses.example: Beyond the twelve-mile limit lies the open ocean.
senses.exampleCN: 越过十二海里界限，就是开阔的公海。
senses.why: maritime law needed a term for water that no flag claims; the everyday word for the great water took that legal slot without changing shape.
senses.whyCN: 海商法需要一个词指没有任何国旗主张的水域，于是日常指大水的词原样填进了这个法律位置。

senses.title: Ocean as a shipping modifier
senses.definition: used before another noun to mean carried by, used on, or belonging to the open sea
senses.definitionCN: 置于名词前，表示由远洋承运、用于远洋或属于远洋的
senses.example: Ocean freight moves most goods between continents.
senses.exampleCN: 远洋货运承担了洲际间的大部分货物。
senses.why: when a noun is placed before another noun it stops naming a place and starts naming a route or a class, which is how ocean becomes the label on a shipping container.
senses.whyCN: 名词放到另一个名词前时，它不再指地点，而开始指一条路线或一个类别，海洋就是这样变成了集装箱上的运输标签。

intro.en: Ocean reaches English through Latin and Old French from Greek Okeanos, the name of the stream that was thought to run around the whole inhabited world. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: ocean 经拉丁语与古法语进入英语，源头是希腊语 Okeanos——古人想象中环绕整个已知世界的大河之名。年代均为约数。

items.en: Okeanos in Homer is the river that encircles the disc of the world and is never crossed; it is a proper name first, a common noun for the outer water later.
items.cn: 荷马笔下的 Okeanos 是环绕世界圆盘、无人能越的大河；它先是专名，后来才成为指外围水域的普通名词。

items.en: Later Greek writers, above all Herodotus, used okeanos for the open water outside the Mediterranean, and the word began to mean the sea itself rather than a river.
items.cn: 后来的希腊作者，尤其是希罗多德，用 okeanos 指地中海之外的开阔水域，这个词开始表示海本身而非一条河。

items.en: Latin took Oceanus as both a name and a common noun for the great sea; the adjective oceanicus 'of the ocean' follows the same stem.
items.cn: 拉丁语把 Oceanus 同时用作专名与指大海洋的普通名词；形容词 oceanicus「海洋的」沿用同一词干。

items.en: Old French occean passed the word to Middle English around the fourteenth century, where it first named the outer sea and only later any large body of salt water.
items.cn: 古法语 occean 在 14 世纪前后把这个词传给中古英语，最初指外围的大海，后来才泛指任何巨大咸水体。

items.en: From the age of exploration the single world water was mapped as named oceans, and the older 'stream around the world' image survives only in poetry and etymology.
items.cn: 从大航海时代起，这一整片世界水域被绘制成有名字的几个大洋，古老「绕世大河」的意象只留在诗歌与词源说明里。

items.en: Source uncertain (root origin, not first date): the deeper origin of Greek Okeanos is disputed, with some scholars treating it as a pre-Greek loan; any reconstructed Indo-European form for it is a hypothesis, not an established derivation.
items.cn: 来源不确定（指词根来源，不是首见年代）：希腊语 Okeanos 的更早来源有争议，有学者视之为前希腊语借词；为它构拟的任何印欧语形式都只是假说，不是已证实的派生。

note.en: Group one holds words that look like ocean or are built on the same stem; group two holds words for water that differ in size or register.
note.cn: 第一组是与 ocean 形近或同出同一词干的词；第二组是都指水域、但规模或语体不同的词。

entries.definition: the collective name for the Pacific islands and Australia; it adds -ia to the Oceanus stem, so it names a region, not a body of water.
entries.definitionCN: 太平洋岛屿与澳大利亚的合称；在 Oceanus 词干上加 -ia，指一个区域，而不是一片水域。

entries.definition: ocean plus -ic: relating to the ocean, or simply very large and open, as in oceanic distances.
entries.definitionCN: ocean 加 -ic：与海洋有关的，或形容极其辽阔开阔的，如「远洋般的距离」。

entries.definition: ocean plus -graphy 'writing, describing': the scientific study of the sea, not the sea itself.
entries.definitionCN: ocean 加 -graphy「书写、描述」：对海洋的科学研究，而不是海洋本身。

entries.definition: ocean plus front: land that faces the sea, so the compound names property rather than water.
entries.definitionCN: ocean 加 front：面朝大海的陆地，因此这个复合词指地产，而非水域。

entries.definition: a body of salt water smaller than an ocean and often partly enclosed by land; the everyday word for the water you can see from a shore.
entries.definitionCN: 比大洋小、常被陆地部分围住的咸水体；指岸边看得见的那片水的日常用词。

entries.definition: a plural used for a particular stretch of water, as in territorial waters; it is neutral in size and common in law and news.
entries.definitionCN: 复数形式，指某一片特定水域，如领海；不限定规模，常见于法律与新闻。

entries.definition: an old poetic word for the open sea, as in the Spanish Main; it survives mostly in verse and historical writing.
entries.definitionCN: 指开阔大海的古雅诗歌用词，如「西班牙海」；如今多存于诗歌与历史写作。

entries.definition: the deep is a literary name for the sea that stresses its depth rather than its width; it fits images of sinking and hiding.
entries.definitionCN: the deep 是海洋的文学称呼，强调深度而非广度；适合「沉没、隐藏」一类意象。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Greek Okeanos was the river around the world, so the word began as one continuous ring of water.
normal.cn: 希腊语 Okeanos 是绕世界的大河，因此这个词最初就是一圈连着的水。

normal.en: The family runs ocean, oceanic, oceanography, oceanographer, oceanarium, oceanfront.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 ocean、oceanic、oceanography、oceanographer、oceanarium、oceanfront。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the physical sense: ocean floor, ocean basin, deep ocean, open ocean.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出物理义：海底、海盆、深海、开阔洋面。

normal.en: Geography names five: the Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern and Arctic oceans.
normal.cn: 地理学列出五个：太平洋、大西洋、印度洋、南大洋与北冰洋。

normal.en: The idiom an ocean of means a huge amount, as in an ocean of paperwork.
normal.cn: 短语 an ocean of 表示极多，如海量文书。

abstract.en: Picture a drop of water that cannot find a shore to belong to.
abstract.cn: 想象一滴水找不到可以归属的岸。

abstract.en: Picture a map where the blue is not a colour but a distance you cannot cross.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图，上面的蓝色不是颜色，而是一段跨不过去的距离。

abstract.en: Picture a voice heard across water, arriving in layers like waves.
abstract.cn: 想象隔着水传来的人声，一层一层像浪一样抵达。

examples.en: The ocean covers about seventy percent of the earth's surface.
examples.cn: 海洋覆盖了地球表面约七成。

examples.en: Scientists track how the ocean moves heat from the tropics poleward.
examples.cn: 科学家追踪海洋如何把热量从热带向极地输送。

examples.en: From the cliff we watched an ocean of cloud roll inland.
examples.cn: 从崖上望去，我们看着一片云海向内陆翻滚。

root: 希腊 Okeanos「环绕世界的大河」（专名转普通名词）→ 拉丁 Oceanus → 古法语 occean → 英语 ocean；Okeanos 的更早来源有争议，或为前希腊语借词，构拟的印欧形式均属假说。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses radiate from one picture: a ring of salt water around the land, then the named parts, the water seen from a ship, the same boundlessness borrowed for quantity and feeling, and finally the water studied as a machine and claimed in law.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从同一个画面辐射出去：环绕陆地的咸水圈，然后是其中命名分区、船上所见的水面，同一份「无边」被借去指数量与情感，最后是当作机器研究的海洋与法律主张的海域。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one continuous ring of salt water holding the land inside it, too wide to see across.
core.cn: 核心意象：一整圈连着的咸水把陆地围在里面，宽到看不见对岸。

branches.en: THE PHYSICAL BODY: the same water is first a place on the map and later a heat store studied by climate science.
branches.cn: 物理水体：同一片水先是地图上的一个地点，后来成为气候科学研究的储热系统。

branches.en: DIVIDED AND CLAIMED: geography cuts the whole into named oceans, and law marks where national claims stop.
branches.cn: 被划分与被主张：地理学把整体切成有名字的洋，法律标出国家主张止于何处。

branches.en: SEEN FROM A SHIP: from deck the water is a setting for travel, and as a modifier it labels the freight that crosses it.
branches.cn: 从船上看见：在甲板上水是旅行的场景，作定语时则标注穿越它的货运。

branches.en: BORROWED SCALE: the widest thing a speaker knows measures paperwork, sand and grass.
branches.cn: 借来的尺度：说话人知道的最宽之物，被用来度量文书、沙与草。

branches.en: INWARD WATER: grief and doubt become oceans because the person is inside them, not beside them.
branches.cn: 向内的水：悲伤与疑虑变成海洋，因为人是在其中，而不是在其旁。

intro.en: Ocean is a borrowed proper name that became a common noun; its family is built with Greek and Latin suffixes added to the same stem.
intro.cn: ocean 是一个转为普通名词的外来专名；它的词族都是在同一词干上加希腊语与拉丁语后缀构成的。

latinIntro.en: Latin Oceanus keeps both the name and the common noun, and oceanicus supplies the adjective pattern behind oceanic.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 Oceanus 同时保留专名与普通名词用法，oceanicus 则提供了 oceanic 背后的形容词构词模式。

definition_en: a preposition marking possession or belonging, the source someone or something comes from, the material a thing is made from, the subject a statement is about, and the amount contained in a measure
core_image: 一只白瓷杯里盛着热茶，杯沿上绕着一缕白气
scene: 午后的厨房很安静，炉上的水刚停，桌上摆着一只白瓷杯和几片切好的柠檬。She poured a cup of tea and left it to cool by the window.

senses.title: Belonging to or connected with
senses.definition: used between two nouns to show that the second belongs to, is part of, or is connected with the first
senses.definitionCN: 用在两个名词之间，表示后者属于、构成或关联于前者
senses.example: The roof of the old house leaked in the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 那座老房子的屋顶在暴风雨中漏了。
senses.why: Old English used the genitive ending on nouns for possession, and of, meaning 'from', gradually took over that work as endings wore away.
senses.whyCN: 古英语靠名词上的属格词尾表示所属，随着词尾逐渐磨损，意为「从……而来」的 of 慢慢接过了这项职能。

senses.title: Coming from a particular source
senses.definition: used after a noun to name the place, person or group that something comes from
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词后，指出某物来自的地方、人或群体
senses.example: She is a teacher of mathematics from a small town.
senses.exampleCN: 她是一位来自小镇的数学老师。
senses.why: The earliest sense of the word was 'away from', so naming where something starts out is one of its oldest jobs.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最早的意思是「离开、从……而来」，所以指出某物的来处是它最古老的职能之一。

senses.title: Made or consisting of a material
senses.definition: used to name the substance a thing is made from or the parts that make it up
senses.definitionCN: 用来指出某物由什么材料制成，或由哪些部分构成
senses.example: The frame is made of bamboo and the seat of woven grass.
senses.exampleCN: 框架由竹子制成，座面则由编草做成。
senses.why: Once of marks where a thing comes from, it can also mark what it was built out of, since material is a kind of origin.
senses.whyCN: 一旦 of 标出某物的来处，它也能标出某物由什么造成，因为材料也是一种来源。

senses.title: About or concerning
senses.definition: used after certain verbs and nouns to introduce the subject that is being thought, spoken or written about
senses.definitionCN: 用在某些动词和名词后，引出被思考、谈论或书写的主题
senses.example: He told us a long story of the sea and its storms.
senses.exampleCN: 他给我们讲了一个关于大海和风暴的长故事。
senses.why: To speak of something is to start from it and move outward in words, so the preposition of source became the marker of a topic.
senses.whyCN: 说到某事物，就是以它为起点用话语向外展开，于是这个表示来源的介词也成了话题的标记。

senses.title: Showing the amount contained in a measure
senses.definition: used between a quantity word or container and the thing it measures, as in a cup of tea or a piece of paper
senses.definitionCN: 用在数量词或容器与它所量的东西之间，如 a cup of tea 或 a piece of paper
senses.example: He asked for a glass of water and a slice of bread.
senses.exampleCN: 他要了一杯水和一片面包。
senses.why: A measure is hollow until something fills it, so of joins the container to its contents and turns two words into one quantity.
senses.whyCN: 度量本身是空的，直到有东西把它填满，于是 of 把容器和内容连起来，让两个词合成一个数量。

intro.en: Of is one of the oldest English words, an unstressed form of a Germanic word meaning 'away from', and its modern uses grew as English lost the noun endings that once marked possession.
intro.cn: of 是英语最古老的词之一，是日耳曼语中表示「离开、从……而来」的词的非重读形式；随着英语丢掉曾经标示所属的名词词尾，它的现代用法才逐渐长成。

items.en: Scholars generally reconstruct a form meaning 'off, away from' behind this family, and the same source is thought to lie behind Greek apo and Latin ab.
items.cn: 学者一般认为这一族词背后有一个表示「离开、从……而来」的形式，并认为希腊语 apo 与拉丁语 ab 也出自同一来源。

items.en: The Germanic form carried the sense of moving away or departing, and it worked as an unstressed preposition rather than a stressed adverb.
items.cn: 日耳曼语形式带着「离开、出发」的意思，且多作非重读介词，而不是重读副词。

items.en: Old English had æf, meaning away or from, alongside of as its weaker, unstressed form in ordinary speech.
items.cn: 古英语有 æf，意为「离开、从」，而 of 是它在日常口语中较弱、非重读的形式。

items.en: Middle English let of take over the possessive work of fading noun endings, so phrases like the roof of the house replaced older inflected forms.
items.cn: 中古英语让 of 接手逐渐消失的名词词尾的所属职能，于是 the roof of the house 这类说法取代了更早的屈折形式。

items.en: Modern English keeps of for possession, source, material, topic and quantity, while its stressed twin off survives as a separate word for departure.
items.cn: 现代英语让 of 承担所属、来源、材料、话题与数量，而它重读的双胞胎 off 作为表示「离开」的独立词留存下来。

note.cn: 形近组收拼写或来历与 of 相近的词；近义组收表示所属或来源的介词与说法。

entries.definition: Away from a place, or not switched on; the stressed twin of of.

entries.definition: An old poetic shortening of often, meaning many times; it is only spelling that resembles of, the source is separate.

entries.definition: Of that or of it, a formal word built by joining there and of.
entries.definitionCN: 关于那一点或它的，由 there 与 of 合成的正式用语。

entries.definitionCN: 标示某物起点或来源的介词。

entries.definitionCN: 引出谈话、思考或写作主题的介词。

entries.definition: A phrase saying what substance something is produced out of.
entries.definitionCN: 表示某物由何种材料制成的说法。

normalIntro.en: Of is a tiny word doing several large jobs at once, and every hook follows the one old idea of starting out from something.
normalIntro.cn: of 是个小词，却同时干着好几件大事，而每条记忆钩子都顺着「从某处出发」这个古老想法。

normal.en: Old English æf meant away or from, and of was simply its light, unstressed form in quick speech.
normal.cn: 古英语 æf 意为「离开、从」，of 只是它在快语速中轻读的形式。

normal.en: Off is the same word under stress, which is why a shop can be off a street and a lid can come off a box.
normal.cn: off 是同一个词的重读形式，所以一家店可以在街道拐出去的位置，盖子也能从盒子上取下来。

normal.en: English once put endings on nouns for possession; as those endings disappeared, of stepped in, giving the roof of the house.
normal.cn: 英语曾在名词上加词尾表示所属；这些词尾消失后，of 补了进来，于是有了 the roof of the house。

normal.en: A cup of tea joins container and contents, so the preposition turns two nouns into one measured amount.
normal.cn: a cup of tea 把容器与内容连在一起，这个介词就把两个名词合成一个被量出的数量。

normal.en: Of course, of mine and think of each freeze a different piece of grammar into a phrase worth learning whole.
normal.cn: of course、of mine 与 think of 各自把一处不同的语法冻成了值得整块记住的说法。

abstract.en: Of is the word English uses when one thing has to be anchored to another, whether by owner, origin, stuff or subject.
abstract.cn: 当一样东西必须拴到另一样上时，英语就动用 of，无论靠的是主人、来处、材料还是话题。

abstract.en: Its history shows a language quietly replacing its own grammar with a small preposition.
abstract.cn: 它的历史显示：一门语言悄悄用一个小介词替换掉了自己原有的语法。

abstract.en: A cup of tea is two nouns and a hinge, which is all most possession really is.
abstract.cn: a cup of tea 是两个名词加一个铰链，而多数「所属」其实也不过如此。

definition_zh: 提供；给予；主动提出；出价；提议；报价；特价
definition_en: to give or present something to someone; to say you are willing to do something; to name a price; as a noun, a proposal, a bid or a special deal
core_image: 双手把东西捧到别人面前，等对方伸手接下
scene: 公交车上人挨着人，一位老人扶着扶手晃了一下，靠窗的年轻人抬手指了指自己旁边的空位。She offered her seat to the old man and he took it with a nod.
sceneCN: 这里 offer 是「提供、让出」（第 1 个义项：把东西给予别人）；句意是她把座位让给了老人，老人点头接受。画面里有拥挤的车厢和一个靠窗的空位。

pos.zh: 提供；给予；主动提出；出价
提议；报价；录用通知；特价

derivatives.zh: 由 offer 加 -ing 构成，义为「献上的东西；祭品；提供的服务或课程」
法律用语，由 offer 加表示「人」的后缀 -or 构成，义为「提出要约的一方」
源自拉丁 offertorium，与 offer 同一词根，义为「礼拜中的奉献环节或奉献金」

senses.title: To give or present something to someone
senses.definition: to give something to someone, especially in a polite or formal way
senses.definitionCN: 尤指以礼貌或正式的方式把某物给予别人
senses.example: She offered him a cup of tea.
senses.exampleCN: 她给他端来一杯茶。
senses.why: Latin offerre meant to bring something before a person, and that picture of presenting an object still drives the first sense.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 offerre 意为把东西带到某人面前，这幅「捧到人前」的画面一直支撑着第一个义项。

senses.title: To say that you are willing to do something
senses.definition: to express willingness to do something for someone
senses.definitionCN: 向别人表示自己愿意做某事
senses.example: He offered to drive us to the station.
senses.exampleCN: 他主动提出开车送我们去车站。
senses.why: Once the thing brought forward can be an action rather than an object, the verb comes to mean putting yourself forward as willing.
senses.whyCN: 当被捧到人前的不再是物件而是一个行动，这个动词就引申为「把自己递上去」，表示愿意效劳。

senses.title: To name a price for something
senses.definition: to say what price you will pay for something or charge for it
senses.definitionCN: 说出你愿意为某物支付、或为某物开出的价钱
senses.example: They offered two million for the house.
senses.exampleCN: 他们出价两百万买那栋房子。
senses.why: In a market the thing brought forward is a sum of money, so presenting turns into bidding.
senses.whyCN: 在市场里，被捧到人前的变成一笔钱，于是「呈上」就转成了「出价」。

senses.title: A proposal or a job offer
senses.definition: a formal proposal, especially one made to be accepted or refused
senses.definitionCN: 正式的提议，尤指摆出来等对方接受或拒绝的那种
senses.example: The company made her an offer she could not refuse.
senses.exampleCN: 公司给了她一个无法拒绝的录用条件。
senses.why: The noun keeps the object that was brought forward, so an offer is the proposal itself, waiting for a yes or a no.
senses.whyCN: 名词保留了那个被捧出来的东西，所以 an offer 就是摆在面前、等人点头或摇头的提议。

senses.title: A special price or deal
senses.definition: a reduced price or a deal advertised to attract buyers
senses.definitionCN: 为吸引买家而宣传的降价价格或优惠方案
senses.example: The shop has a special offer on coffee this week.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店本周咖啡有特价。
senses.why: When a price is put in front of a buyer as a bargain, the same noun narrows to the attractive deal on the label.
senses.whyCN: 当价格作为便宜货摆到买家面前，同一个名词就收窄为标签上那个吸引人的优惠。

intro.en: Offer goes back to a Latin verb meaning to bring before, was borrowed early into Old English for sacrifice, and was then widened by French to any kind of presenting.
intro.cn: offer 可追到拉丁语中意为「带到面前」的动词，早期借入古英语时指献祭，后经法语扩展为一切形式的呈上。

items.en: Offerre joined ob-, meaning toward or before, with ferre, meaning to bring, so it meant to bring something before someone.
items.cn: offerre 把表示「向前、对着」的 ob- 与表示「带来、搬运」的 ferre 合在一起，意为把东西带到某人面前。

items.en: Old English borrowed the Latin verb early as offrian, and its first use was bringing a sacrifice before God.
items.cn: 古英语早期就把这个拉丁动词借进来写作 offrian，最初用于把祭品献到神面前。

items.en: Norman French offrir reinforced the word and widened it from sacrifice to any act of presenting.
items.cn: 诺曼法语 offrir 重新加固了这个词，并把「献祭」扩展为任何形式的呈上。

items.en: Middle English offer covered presenting gifts, making a proposal and naming a price.
items.cn: 中古英语的 offer 已覆盖呈上礼物、提出建议与开出价钱。

items.en: Modern English keeps the religious echo in offering and offertory, and the commercial sense in bid and special offer.
items.cn: 现代英语在 offering 与 offertory 里保留宗教余音，在出价与特价里保留商业含义。

note.cn: 形近组收派生词以及同样建立在拉丁语「搬运」动词上的词；近义组收表示给予、提议与出价的动词。
